chunks: And ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Do not swear by Allah, whether truthfully or falsely, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has indeed forbidden that, so He, Mighty and Majestic, said:"
"And do not make Allah an object of your oaths."

key_terms.بِاللَّهِ: by Allah; invoking the Divine Name in an oath
key_terms.تَحْلِفُوا: to swear or take an oath
key_terms.عُرْضَةً: something made subject to frequent use or exposure; an object/pretext in oaths

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about swearing oaths by Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith forbids frequent or casual swearing by Allah, whether one is truthful or lying. It supports this ruling by citing the Qur'anic prohibition against making Allah a pretext or object in one's oaths, emphasizing reverence for the Divine Name.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4281 - Uthman ibn Isa narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (as), who said:
"Do not swear by Allah (swt), whether truthfully or falsely, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, has forbidden that, as He (swt), the Almighty, says:
'And do not make Allah (swt) an excuse in your oaths' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:224)."
